scalar_search.integrality_proof: For central returns, the common A1 root has product-1 with both framing roots. Its triangular cyclic product is g. Thus arithmetic cyclic-product integrality implies g belongs to the full ring of integers Z[phi]; this is not inferred from norm-two normalization alone.

central_edge_endpoint_census.completeness: The new root belongs to exactly one finite component. Deleting it gives a submultiset of the fixed common components; all other components stay unchanged. Exhausting all rooted finite components through rank21 therefore exhausts every completion type and every incoming port.

selected_facet_incidence.proof: At a vertex on the selected narrow facet F, every central E8 port except possibly the facet normal gives an edge lying in F. Its framing pair has minimality14. The opposite endpoint cannot again have type D5+2E8. Count these edges at their nonexceptional ends; their common diagram is S, so each endpoint of type U receives at most m(U)<=4. Every edge counted has exactly one exceptional endpoint.
selected_facet_incidence.applicability: Only vertices and edges of the chosen narrow facet. No constraint on whole-polytope vertex frequencies is asserted. The theorem does not force a selected triangle/quadrilateral to meet these central ports.
